nodes.theorem_title: Reduced journeys preserve the movement constraints
nodes.formal_statement: theorem AngelDevil.reducedJourney_is_journey (p : Nat) (h : List AngelDevil.Point) (hj : AngelDevil.Journey p h) : AngelDevil.Journey p (AngelDevil.reducedJourney p h) := by sorry
nodes.natural_language_statement: For any nonnegative integer power and any finite journey starting at the origin with each coordinate changing by at most that power per step, the earliest-predecessor reduction is again a journey with the same movement constraint. This states the structural validity of the reduction; the separate assertion about avoiding squares eaten by the transformed Devil is not included.
nodes.source: Mathe, The Angel of power 2 wins (2007), https://doi.org/10.1017/S0963548306008303, author manuscript p. 3, equation (1) and the paragraph immediately following it.

nodes.theorem_title: Claim 2.1 and determinacy: a uniform confinement box
nodes.formal_statement:
theorem AngelDevil.uniform_confinement (p : Nat) (hp : 0 < p)
    (h : ¬ AngelWins p) : ∃ N, 0 < N ∧ ∃ D : DevilStrategy,
    ∀ A n, (∀ m, m < n →
      Jump p (current (play A D m)) (current (play A D (m+1))) ∧
      some (current (play A D (m+1))) ∉ (play A D (m+1)).burned) →
      InBox N (current (play A D n)) := by sorry
nodes.natural_language_statement: For each positive integer power, if no single Angel strategy survives against every Devil, there is a positive integer radius and one Devil strategy such that every safe finite play remains inside that box. The radius and Devil are chosen before the Angel strategy and play length. This target includes the introductory determinacy observation as well as Claim 2.1; neither is assumed as an extra hypothesis.
nodes.source: Andras Mathe, The Angel of power 2 wins, CPC 16 (2007), 363-374; https://doi.org/10.1017/S0963548306008303; author manuscript internal pagination. Claim 2.1, p. 2, and the introductory determinacy observation, p. 1.

nodes.theorem_title: No-return of the wall trace implies the Nice Angel theorem
nodes.formal_statement: theorem AngelDevil.niceAngelWins_of_wall_no_return (hreturn : ∀ D, AngelDevil.Nice 2 D → ∀ n, 0 < n → AngelDevil.wallTrace D n ≠ AngelDevil.initialWall) : AngelDevil.NiceAngelWins 2 := by sorry
nodes.natural_language_statement: Assume that against every Nice Devil, the specified two-transition wall trace never returns to its initial directed wall at a positive index. Then there is one power-two Angel strategy that survives against every Nice Devil and, against each such Devil, leaves every finite box centered at the origin. The no-return premise is an explicit geometric assumption; this conditional theorem does not by itself establish that premise.
nodes.source: Mathe, The Angel of power 2 wins (2007), https://doi.org/10.1017/S0963548306008303; author manuscript pp. 6-8, octagonal wall-following rule, Claim 3.1 analogue, Proposition 4.3 and Theorem 4.5. Two wall transitions per turn give an admissible power-two implementation; no-return is the remaining geometric obligation.

nodes.theorem_title: Side-connected integer squares and their unit boundary
nodes.natural_language_statement: Squares are indexed by integer pairs. The four side neighbors differ by one in exactly one coordinate. A finite set is connected when it is nonempty and any two members can be joined by a finite sequence of side-neighbor steps within the set. Each exposed side is a direction from an occupied square to an unoccupied neighbor. The perimeter counts all such sides, including hole boundaries. The wall set records the occupied square and side direction.
nodes.source: Mathe, The Angel of power 2 wins (2007), https://doi.org/10.1017/S0963548306008303, author manuscript p. 6, Definition 4.1 and Claim 4.2.

nodes.theorem_title: Theorem 2.4: transfer confinement to a Nice Devil
nodes.formal_statement:
theorem AngelDevil.confinement_to_nice (p N : Nat) (D : DevilStrategy)
    (hc : ∀ A n, (∀ m, m < n →
      Jump p (current (play A D m)) (current (play A D (m+1))) ∧
      some (current (play A D (m+1))) ∉ (play A D (m+1)).burned) →
      InBox N (current (play A D n))) : NiceCanConfine p N  := by sorry
nodes.natural_language_statement: Let p and N be nonnegative integers. If a Devil strategy keeps every safe finite play of the power-p Angel inside the box of radius N, then some Nice Devil does the same. The assumption ranges over every Angel strategy and every finite time, requiring safety only up to that time. This formalization includes the degenerate cases p = 0 and N = 0 in addition to the positive parameters in the paper.
nodes.source: Andras Mathe, The Angel of power 2 wins, CPC 16 (2007), 363-374; https://doi.org/10.1017/S0963548306008303; author manuscript internal pagination. Theorem 2.4, pp. 2-3, with harmless zero-parameter extension.

nodes.theorem_title: Theorem 4.6: the Angel of power two wins
nodes.natural_language_statement: There exists a single power-two Angel strategy that makes legal uneaten landings forever against every Devil strategy on the infinite integer lattice, with the Devil moving first and permitted to pass.
nodes.source: Andras Mathe, The Angel of power 2 wins, CPC 16 (2007), 363-374; https://doi.org/10.1017/S0963548306008303; author manuscript internal pagination. Theorem 4.6, manuscript p. 8.

nodes.formal_statement:
theorem AngelDevil.finite_game_determined (p T : Nat) :
    FiniteAngelWins p T ∨ ∃ D, ∀ A, ¬ SafeFor p A D T := by sorry
nodes.natural_language_statement: For every nonnegative power p and finite horizon T, either one Angel strategy is safe for T rounds against every Devil, or one Devil strategy prevents every Angel strategy from being safe for T rounds. Both strategies use the original history interfaces. At horizon zero the first alternative holds. This is the finite-horizon determinacy step used with compactness in the confinement argument.
nodes.source: Mathe, The Angel of power 2 wins (2007), https://doi.org/10.1017/S0963548306008303, author manuscript pp. 1-2, determinacy observation and Claim 2.1 proof; finite-horizon intermediate statement.

nodes.theorem_title: Theorem 2.7: reduction to a Nice Devil
nodes.formal_statement: theorem AngelDevil.nice_devil_reduction (p : Nat) (hp : 0 < p) : ¬ AngelDevil.AngelWins p → ∃ N, 0 < N ∧ AngelDevil.NiceCanConfine p N := by sorry
nodes.natural_language_statement: For every positive integer power, if the Angel has no winning strategy, some Nice Devil can keep every finite safe play in a fixed box of positive integer radius. This formulation includes the determinacy observation from the introduction in addition to Theorem 2.7.
nodes.source: Andras Mathe, The Angel of power 2 wins, CPC 16 (2007), 363-374; https://doi.org/10.1017/S0963548306008303; author manuscript internal pagination. Theorem 2.7, manuscript p. 3, with the introductory determinacy observation on p. 1.

nodes.theorem_title: Geometric no-return for the power-two wall trace
nodes.formal_statement: theorem AngelDevil.wallTrace_never_returns (D : AngelDevil.DevilStrategy) (hnice : AngelDevil.Nice 2 D) (n : Nat) (hn : 0 < n) : AngelDevil.wallTrace D n ≠ AngelDevil.initialWall := by sorry
nodes.natural_language_statement: Against every Nice Devil of power two, the specified boundary-walking strategy never encounters its initial directed wall at any positive wall-transition index. The initial wall is the east side of square (-1,0). The trace uses two wall transitions per Angel turn and the obstacle set after that turn's Devil move. This is the geometric no-return obligation underlying the escape argument; it does not assume non-repetition or escape.
nodes.source: Mathe, The Angel of power 2 wins (2007), https://doi.org/10.1017/S0963548306008303; author manuscript pp. 6-8, octagonal wall-following rule, Claim 3.1 analogue, Proposition 4.3 and Theorem 4.5. Two wall transitions per turn give an admissible power-two implementation; no-return is the remaining geometric obligation.

nodes.theorem_title: Octagonal boundary walk and the power-two wall strategy
nodes.natural_language_statement: A directed wall is an occupied integer square with an outward side direction. The tangent points counterclockwise from the outward normal. To advance, first test the occupied square's tangent neighbor: if empty, turn around the same square, even when the diagonal square is occupied. Otherwise test the diagonal square: if empty, continue straight; if occupied, turn around the concave corner. Obstacles consist of all squares with negative first coordinate together with the recorded Devil choices. Starting with the east side of square (-1,0), the strategy performs exactly two wall transitions after each Devil move and lands in the outside square. Its state is reconstructed from the chronological burn history. The wall trace records individual transitions, using the same obstacle set for both transitions of a round.
nodes.definition:
import Definitions.Def_AngelDevil_SquareBoundary

namespace AngelDevil

abbrev Wall := Point × SquareSide

/-- Counterclockwise rotation of the outward normal: occupied squares are left. -/
def tangentSide (d : SquareSide) : SquareSide :=
  (!d.1, if d.1 then !d.2 else d.2)

def wallOutside (w : Wall) : Point := sideNeighbor w.1 w.2

def IsBoundaryWall (B : Set Point) (w : Wall) : Prop :=
  w.1 ∈ B ∧ wallOutside w ∉ B

/-- The corner rule for shrunken blocks. An empty side-neighbor takes
priority over a diagonally touching block, so the walker passes through the gap. -/
noncomputable def nextWall (B : Set Point) (w : Wall) : Wall := by
  classical
  let t := tangentSide w.2
  let a := sideNeighbor w.1 t
  let b := sideNeighbor a w.2
  exact if a ∉ B then (w.1, t)
    else if b ∉ B then (a, w.2)
    else (b, oppositeSide t)

noncomputable def previousWall (B : Set Point) (w : Wall) : Wall := by
  classical
  let t := oppositeSide (tangentSide w.2)
  let a := sideNeighbor w.1 t
  let b := sideNeighbor a w.2
  exact if a ∉ B then (w.1, t)
    else if b ∉ B then (a, w.2)
    else (b, oppositeSide t)

def initialWall : Wall := ((-1, 0), (false, false))

def wallObstacles (burned : List (Option Point)) : Set Point :=
  {v | v.1 < 0 ∨ some v ∈ burned}

/-- Two wall transitions per turn fit inside the power-two movement box. -/
noncomputable def wallHistory (burned : List (Option Point)) : Wall :=
  if _h : burned = [] then initialWall else
  let w := wallHistory burned.dropLast
  nextWall (wallObstacles burned) (nextWall (wallObstacles burned) w)
termination_by burned.length
decreasing_by
  have hp := List.length_pos_iff.mpr _h
  simp only [List.length_dropLast]
  omega

noncomputable def wallAngel : AngelStrategy :=
  fun _ burned => wallOutside (wallHistory burned)

def traceObstacles (D : DevilStrategy) (i : Nat) : Set Point :=
  wallObstacles (play wallAngel D (i / 2 + 1)).burned

noncomputable def wallTrace (D : DevilStrategy) : Nat → Wall
  | 0 => initialWall
  | i+1 => nextWall (traceObstacles D i) (wallTrace D i)

end AngelDevil
nodes.source: Mathe, The Angel of power 2 wins (2007), https://doi.org/10.1017/S0963548306008303; author manuscript pp. 6-8, octagonal wall-following rule, Claim 3.1 analogue, Proposition 4.3 and Theorem 4.5. Two wall transitions per turn give an admissible power-two implementation; no-return is the remaining geometric obligation.

nodes.theorem_title: Earliest-predecessor reduction of finite Angel journeys
nodes.natural_language_statement: A total recursive implementation of the reduced journey in Mathe Section 2, equation (1). At each endpoint it chooses the earliest reachable predecessor in the original prefix, recursively reduces that prefix, and appends the endpoint. Empty and malformed histories have explicit fallback cases; proved correctness for valid journeys is a separate theorem.
nodes.definition:
import Definitions.Def_AngelDevil_Game

namespace AngelDevil

instance jumpDecidable (p : Nat) (u v : Point) : Decidable (Jump p u v) := by
  unfold Jump
  infer_instance

def firstReachable (p : Nat) (h : List Point) (z : Point) : Nat :=
  h.findIdx (fun v => decide (Jump p v z))

/- Section 2, equation (1). The recursive predecessor is the earliest point in
the ORIGINAL prefix that can reach the endpoint, not an arbitrary loop erasure.
The singleton fallback only specifies a total function on malformed journeys.
-/
def reducedJourney (p : Nat) (h : List Point) : List Point :=
  if _hnil : h = [] then [] else
  let z := h.getLastD origin
  if z = origin then [origin] else
  let prior := h.dropLast
  let i := firstReachable p prior z
  if i < prior.length then
    reducedJourney p (prior.take (i+1)) ++ [z]
  else [z]
termination_by h.length
decreasing_by
  have hpos : 0 < h.length := List.length_pos_iff.mpr _hnil
  simp only [List.length_take, List.length_dropLast]
  omega

end AngelDevil
nodes.source: Mathe, The Angel of power 2 wins (2007), https://doi.org/10.1017/S0963548306008303, author manuscript p. 3, equation (1).

nodes.theorem_title: Theorem 4.5: power two escapes every Nice Devil
nodes.natural_language_statement: There exists one power-two Angel strategy that survives against every Nice Devil and, against each such opponent, reaches outside every finite box centred at the origin.
nodes.source: Andras Mathe, The Angel of power 2 wins, CPC 16 (2007), 363-374; https://doi.org/10.1017/S0963548306008303; author manuscript internal pagination. Theorem 4.5, manuscript p. 8.

nodes.theorem_title: Angel and Devil: infinite-board game and strategies
nodes.natural_language_statement: Integer lattice game with Devil-first rounds, passing, history-dependent strategies, legal survival, Nice Devil restrictions, unbounded escape, and confinement of every finite safe prefix. Conventions follow Sections 1-2, Definitions 2.2, 2.3, 2.5 and equation (2).
nodes.definition:
import Std

/-! The convention is Mathe's paper: Devil moves first, may pass, and may
eat any square (including the occupied square); only subsequent landing on
an eaten square loses. Zero-length Angel moves are allowed by Definition 2.5.
Histories are stored oldest first. Strategies are total also off legal play.
-/
namespace AngelDevil

abbrev Point := Int × Int
def origin : Point := (0, 0)

def Jump (p : Nat) (u v : Point) : Prop :=
  -(p : Int) ≤ v.1 - u.1 ∧ v.1 - u.1 ≤ (p : Int) ∧
  -(p : Int) ≤ v.2 - u.2 ∧ v.2 - u.2 ≤ (p : Int)

def InBox (N : Nat) (v : Point) : Prop := Jump N origin v

def Journey (p : Nat) (h : List Point) : Prop :=
  h.head? = some origin ∧
  ∀ (i : Nat) (u v : Point), h[i]? = some u → h[i+1]? = some v → Jump p u v

abbrev DevilStrategy := List Point → Option Point
abbrev AngelStrategy := List Point → List (Option Point) → Point

structure State where
  visited : List Point
  burned : List (Option Point)

def initial : State := ⟨[origin], []⟩
def current (s : State) : Point := s.visited.getLastD origin
def step (A : AngelStrategy) (D : DevilStrategy) (s : State) : State :=
  let burned := s.burned ++ [D s.visited]
  ⟨s.visited ++ [A s.visited burned], burned⟩

def play (A : AngelStrategy) (D : DevilStrategy) : Nat → State
  | 0 => initial
  | n+1 => step A D (play A D n)

def Survives (p : Nat) (A : AngelStrategy) (D : DevilStrategy) : Prop :=
  ∀ n, Jump p (current (play A D n)) (current (play A D (n+1))) ∧
    some (current (play A D (n+1))) ∉ (play A D (n+1)).burned

def AngelWins (p : Nat) : Prop := ∃ A, ∀ D, Survives p A D

/- Definition 2.2, as made explicit by equation (2): the origin and every
square reachable from a position before the last one are protected. -/
def Nice (p : Nat) (D : DevilStrategy) : Prop :=
  ∀ h, Journey p h → ∀ z, D h = some z →
    z ≠ origin ∧ ∀ v ∈ h.dropLast, ¬ Jump p v z

def Escapes (A : AngelStrategy) (D : DevilStrategy) : Prop :=
  ∀ N : Nat, ∃ n : Nat, ¬ InBox N (current (play A D n))

def NiceAngelWins (p : Nat) : Prop :=
  ∃ A, ∀ D, Nice p D → Survives p A D ∧ Escapes A D

def NiceCanConfine (p N : Nat) : Prop :=
  ∃ D, Nice p D ∧ ∀ A n,
    (∀ m, m < n →
      Jump p (current (play A D m)) (current (play A D (m+1))) ∧
      some (current (play A D (m+1))) ∉ (play A D (m+1)).burned) →
    InBox N (current (play A D n))

end AngelDevil
nodes.source: Andras Mathe, The Angel of power 2 wins, CPC 16 (2007), 363-374; https://doi.org/10.1017/S0963548306008303; author manuscript internal pagination. Sections 1-2, manuscript pp. 1-3.

nodes.theorem_title: Finite-horizon safety and bounded Angel moves
nodes.natural_language_statement: Safety for n rounds requires every one of the first n jumps to be legal and to avoid all squares selected so far. Finite-horizon winning means one Angel strategy is safe for that horizon against every Devil. Strategy inputs are visited and burned histories. Legal displacements are encoded by pairs of integers from 0 through 2p, translated by minus p in each coordinate. The encoding retains legal choices and replaces illegal choices by staying put.
nodes.definition:
import Definitions.Def_AngelDevil_Game

namespace AngelDevil

def SafeFor (p : Nat) (A : AngelStrategy) (D : DevilStrategy) (n : Nat) : Prop :=
  ∀ m, m < n →
    Jump p (current (play A D m)) (current (play A D (m+1))) ∧
    some (current (play A D (m+1))) ∉ (play A D (m+1)).burned

def FiniteAngelWins (p n : Nat) : Prop := ∃ A, ∀ D, SafeFor p A D n

abbrev Observation := List Point × List (Option Point)
abbrev BoundedMove (p : Nat) := Fin (2*p+1) × Fin (2*p+1)

def decodeMove (p : Nat) (h : List Point) (d : BoundedMove p) : Point :=
  ((h.getLastD origin).1 + (d.1.val : Int) - (p : Int),
   (h.getLastD origin).2 + (d.2.val : Int) - (p : Int))

def boundedAngel (p : Nat) (f : Observation → BoundedMove p) : AngelStrategy :=
  fun h b => decodeMove p h (f (h, b))

/- Invalid off-path choices are replaced by staying put. Legal choices are
encoded exactly, so this changes no safe finite play. -/
noncomputable def encodeAngel (p : Nat) (A : AngelStrategy) :
    Observation → BoundedMove p := by
  classical
  intro o
  let v := A o.1 o.2
  let u := o.1.getLastD origin
  exact if hv : Jump p u v then
    (⟨(v.1-u.1+(p : Int)).toNat, by unfold Jump at hv; omega⟩,
     ⟨(v.2-u.2+(p : Int)).toNat, by unfold Jump at hv; omega⟩)
  else (⟨p, by omega⟩, ⟨p, by omega⟩)

end AngelDevil
nodes.source: Mathe, The Angel of power 2 wins (2007), https://doi.org/10.1017/S0963548306008303, author manuscript pp. 1-2: determinacy observation and Claim 2.1; auxiliary formalization definitions.

nodes.theorem_title: Finite-horizon survival yields an infinite winning strategy
nodes.formal_statement:
theorem AngelDevil.finite_survival_compactness (p : Nat)
    (hf : ∀ n, FiniteAngelWins p n) : AngelWins p := by sorry
nodes.natural_language_statement: For any nonnegative integer power, suppose that for every finite number n of rounds there exists an Angel strategy that remains safe for n rounds against every Devil. Then a single Angel strategy remains safe forever against every Devil. The finite strategies may depend on n; the conclusion uses one strategy for all rounds.
nodes.source: Mathe, The Angel of power 2 wins (2007), https://doi.org/10.1017/S0963548306008303, author manuscript p. 2, Claim 2.1 proof: the suitable limit of finite-horizon strategies.

nodes.theorem_title: Claim 2.6: allowed journeys remain allowed after reduction
nodes.formal_statement:
theorem AngelDevil.reducedJourney_allowed (p : Nat) (D : DevilStrategy) (h : List Point)
    (ha : Allowed p (niceReduction p D) h) : Allowed p D (reducedJourney p h)  := by sorry
nodes.natural_language_statement: For every nonnegative integer power, every Devil strategy and every finite journey allowed against its Nice transformation, the reduced journey is allowed against the original Devil. Allowedness includes both bounded jumps and avoidance of all earlier Devil selections. The statement also covers power zero.
nodes.source: Andras Mathe, The Angel of power 2 wins, CPC 16 (2007), 363-374; https://doi.org/10.1017/S0963548306008303; author manuscript internal pagination. Claim 2.6, p. 3.

nodes.theorem_title: Nice Devil transformation and allowed finite journeys
nodes.natural_language_statement: For a finite history, a square is eligible for a Nice Devil precisely when it is not the origin and is outside the power-p neighbourhood of every position except the last. The transformed Devil applies the original Devil to the reduced history, and retains its selected square exactly when eligible; otherwise it passes. An allowed journey starts at the origin, has legal jumps, and never lands on any square selected by the Devil at an earlier prefix, including the selection immediately before landing.
nodes.definition:
import Definitions.Def_AngelDevil_ReducedJourney

namespace AngelDevil

/- Equation (2): protect the origin and the neighbourhood of every position
strictly before the current one. The Devil may still eat the current position
when it is not protected by an earlier position. -/
def NiceEligible (p : Nat) (h : List Point) (z : Point) : Prop :=
  z ≠ origin ∧ ∀ v ∈ h.dropLast, ¬ Jump p v z

instance niceEligibleDecidable (p : Nat) (h : List Point) (z : Point) :
    Decidable (NiceEligible p h z) := by
  unfold NiceEligible
  infer_instance

def niceReduction (p : Nat) (D : DevilStrategy) : DevilStrategy := fun h =>
  match D (reducedJourney p h) with
  | none => none
  | some z => if NiceEligible p h z then some z else none

/- An allowed finite journey: the Devil acts on prefix i before landing j,
so all pairs i < j must be checked, not only consecutive moves. -/
def Allowed (p : Nat) (D : DevilStrategy) (h : List Point) : Prop :=
  Journey p h ∧ ∀ (i j : Nat) (z : Point), i < j → h[j]? = some z →
    D (h.take (i+1)) ≠ some z

end AngelDevil
nodes.source: Andras Mathe, The Angel of power 2 wins, CPC 16 (2007), 363-374; https://doi.org/10.1017/S0963548306008303; author manuscript internal pagination. Definition 2.5 and following discussion, p. 2; equation (2), p. 3.

nodes.explanation:
This proves the confinement transfer of Mathe's Theorem 2.4, also allowing zero
power or zero box radius. It uses Claim 2.6 as a published theorem dependency.

First, any allowed finite history can be realized by a scripted Angel strategy.
Conversely, every safe prefix of strategy play is an allowed history. This proves
equivalence of history-based confinement and the finite-safe-prefix confinement
used by the mission. Apply the original confinement hypothesis to the reduced
history, which is allowed by Claim 2.6. The reduction preserves its endpoint.
Equation (2) gives a Nice Devil, so its finite safe plays stay in the same box.

No determinacy or existence of a uniform confinement box is asserted here.
Those remain separate obligations for Theorem 2.7.

Theorem 2.7 follows from a uniform confinement box for an unrestricted Devil
(Claim 2.1 plus the introductory determinacy observation) and the confinement
transfer of Theorem 2.4. The latter is proved; the former remains an open target.
This submission is a genuine dependency decomposition, not a completed proof
of Theorem 2.7 while uniform confinement remains open.

This proves Mathe's Claim 2.6 using the equation (2) transformation.

Induct along the recursive earliest-predecessor construction. Every nonempty
prefix of a reduced journey is the reduction of some original prefix. If the
last vertex is not the origin, every original position strictly before its
earliest predecessor is too far away to protect that last vertex under the
Nice filter. A Devil selection of this last vertex on any reduced prefix would
therefore also be made by the transformed Devil on the corresponding original
prefix, contradicting allowedness. Earlier reduced landings are handled by the
induction hypothesis. Origin-ending histories reduce to a singleton.

The submitted proof imports and uses the published preservation-of-Journey
theorem `09953273-0806-4e9f-a1da-0b10a2292ffb`. The closed local proof also builds
independently without importing any open platform theorem placeholders.

Assuming the two paper milestones, the Angel of power two has a winning strategy.
The child statements are open obligations, not conclusions established by this
submission.

Suppose there were no winning power-two Angel strategy. Theorem 2.7, in the
formulation that includes the introduction's determinacy observation, supplies a
positive radius and a Nice Devil that confines every finite safe play to that box.
Theorem 4.5 supplies a single Angel strategy that survives and escapes every box
against every Nice Devil. Apply this strategy to the confining Nice Devil.

Its infinite survival makes each finite prefix safe. Its escape property supplies
a round outside the confining box, while the confinement property places that same
round inside the box. This contradiction proves the main conclusion conditional
on the two imported milestones. This is the last deduction on manuscript page 8,
after Theorem 4.5.

The original NiceAngelWins 2 target follows from the proved conditional implication niceAngelWins_of_wall_no_return and the explicit geometric child wallTrace_never_returns. The implication supplies one concrete power-two strategy, survival, the first-repeat argument, and finite-box escape. The no-return child remains open; this is a reduction, not a completed proof of the Nice Angel theorem.

This proves the original uniform-confinement target, combining the introductory
determinacy observation and Claim 2.1. If the Angel has no infinite winning
strategy, finite-survival compactness gives a finite horizon with no universally
safe Angel strategy. Finite-game determinacy then gives one Devil forcing
failure by that horizon T.

A safe n-round play moves at most np in each coordinate. Under this Devil, any
safe prefix must have n < T, so all safe prefixes lie in the positive-radius box
B(Tp+1). The proof imports and uses the independently verified compactness and
finite-determinacy statements, and keeps the original theorem's quantifiers.
